subject: general
question: Which article of the Indian Constitution relates RTI to the fundamental right to freedom of speech and expression?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 19(1)(a)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Article 19(1)(a)** of the Indian Constitution guarantees the **fundamental right to freedom of speech and expression** to all citizens of India.
 
• In the landmark judgment of **Union of India vs. Association for Democratic Reforms (2002)**, the Supreme Court of India held that the **Right to Information (RTI) is intrinsic to freedom of speech and expression** under Article 19(1)(a).
 
• The **RTI Act, 2005** was enacted by Parliament to empower citizens to request information from public authorities, ensuring transparency and accountability in governance.
 
• RTI strengthens the democratic process by enabling citizens to actively participate in governance and decision-making processes.
 
• The provision under Article 19(1)(a) ensures that citizens can access **public records, policies, and decisions** to make informed opinions, which is a crucial aspect of democratic societies.
